name: Edom, in the day of his brother
charge: Standing on the other side in the day that strangers carried away Jacob captive, and being as one of them; rejoicing over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction; entering the gate, laying hands on the substance, standing in the crossway to cut off those that escaped, and delivering up those that remained
summary: Obadiah’s vision is one charge against Edom: when strangers carried Jacob captive and cast lots on Jerusalem, Esau stood on the other side and was as one of them, rejoicing over Judah, looting the gate, cutting off those who escaped and handing over the survivors (Obadiah 1:10-14). The Lord would bring the proud eagle down from its nest among the stars, return his deeds on his own head, and make the house of Esau stubble for the fire of Jacob (Obadiah 1:4; Obadiah 1:15; Obadiah 1:18). The study note and the classes identify Edom as Esau, the white man (Genesis 36:1; Genesis 36:8).
offenseFull: The Lord has made Edom small among the heathen and greatly despised (Obadiah 1:1-2). Esau is Edom, the study note says, and Edom is the white man, called red for his lack of melanin, while Jacob needed no description (Genesis 36:1). The pride of his heart deceived him, dwelling in the clefts of the rock and asking who would bring him down (Obadiah 1:3). The teachers read the clefts together: Mount Seir, where Esau dwelt (Genesis 36:8); the rock-cut city of Petra; the Caucasus mountains of the Middle Ages, which is why they call themselves Caucasian; and today the governments, the high places and the skyscrapers. He exalts himself as the eagle and sets his nest among the stars (Obadiah 1:4): Rome, Greece, Spain, France, Britain, Russia and America take the eagle for their symbol, the great seal holding arrows and an olive branch, and the nest among the stars is the moon landing, the satellites and the space force; in 1969 they said the eagle has landed.

A thief steals until he has enough, and grape gatherers leave some grapes (Obadiah 1:5), but Esau, the class says, takes every grape, the stem, the root and the ground, the house, the people in the house, the land, the race and the identity; like the ocean, he is never full. His hidden things will be searched out (Obadiah 1:6), and God puts His spirit on us to search them out. The class answers from the record why he is greatly despised: the papal bulls Dum Diversas and Romanus Pontifex granted perpetual slavery over all who were not European, and perpetual slavery is perpetual hatred; then the Force Publique in the Congo and the massacres at Ponce and Utuado.

The charge is his violence against his brother Jacob (Obadiah 1:10). In the day strangers carried away Jacob’s forces and cast lots on Jerusalem, Esau stood on the other side and took part, the study note says (Obadiah 1:11). The class teaches that Edom aided the Babylonians, who were Cushites, in the destruction of the first temple in 586 BC, and Esdras says the Edomites burned the temple when the Chaldees laid Judea waste (1 Esdras 4:45). He looked on the day of his brother, rejoiced over Judah in the day of its destruction, entered the gate and laid hands on its substance, and stood in the crossway to cut off those who escaped and hand over the rest (Obadiah 1:12-14): when we were escaping, Edom blocked our way and gave us up. Psalm 137 remembers the children of Edom crying to raze Jerusalem to its foundation (Psalm 137:7). Ezekiel names the same revenge (Ezekiel 25:12), and the class says he takes it through the legislative, judicial and executive branches, weaponizing the police, the original slave catchers.
judgmentFull: From his nest among the stars the Lord will bring him down (Obadiah 1:4): once you reach that height, the class says, the bringing down begins, and from 1969 the teachings started going out. The men of his confederacy will deceive him and bring him to the border, and those who eat his bread will lay a wound under him (Obadiah 1:7); the classes name the European Union and NATO, and the Obadiah teaching the ten horns that turn on the harlot (Revelation 17:12-17): his own confederacy turns on him, as it did in the world wars. The wise will perish out of Edom and the mighty men of Teman be dismayed, and for his violence against Jacob shame will cover him (Obadiah 1:8-10).

The day of the Lord is near on all the heathen: as he has done, it will be done to him (Obadiah 1:15). That is justice, the class says; their reward is what they did to us. The nations will drink and be as though they had not been (Obadiah 1:16), which one class carries from America to those who came back to the land in 1948. On Mount Zion there will be deliverance, and the house of Jacob will be a fire, Joseph a flame, and Esau stubble, with none remaining (Obadiah 1:17-18). Ezekiel says the Lord will lay His vengeance on Edom by the hand of His people Israel (Ezekiel 25:13-14), and the study note says that vengeance is future: the Most High must first change our minds (Zechariah 9:13; Wisdom 3:6-8). It is written because we are soft, the class adds; the day is coming, but now is not that time. The Obadiah teaching warns that we are not to walk around with actual hatred, only to remember our history. Saviours will come up on Mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau, and the kingdom will be the Lord’s (Obadiah 1:21); we are the herald to Christ, the class says.

text.text: For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever.

In the day that thou stoodest on the other side, in the day that the strangers carried away captive his forces, and foreigners entered into his gates, and cast lots upon Jerusalem, even thou wast as one of them.

But thou shouldest not have looked on the day of thy brother in the day that he became a stranger; neither shouldest thou have rejoiced over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction; neither shouldest thou have spoken proudly in the day of distress.

Thou shouldest not have entered into the gate of my people in the day of their calamity; yea, thou shouldest not have looked on their affliction in the day of their calamity, nor have laid hands on their substance in the day of their calamity;
Neither shouldest thou have stood in the crossway, to cut off those of his that did escape; neither shouldest thou have delivered up those of his that did remain in the day of distress.
Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars, thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord.
For the day of the Lord is near upon all the heathen: as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head.

And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble, and they shall kindle in them, and devour them; and there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau; for the Lord hath spoken it.
Now these are the generations of Esau, who is Edom.
Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.
The vision of Obadiah. Thus saith the Lord God concerning Edom; We have heard a rumour from the Lord, and an ambassador is sent among the heathen, Arise ye, and let us rise up against her in battle.
Behold, I have made thee small among the heathen: thou art greatly despised.
The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?
If thieves came to thee, if robbers by night, (how art thou cut off!) would they not have stolen till they had enough? if the grapegatherers came to thee, would they not leave some grapes?
How are the things of Esau searched out! how are his hidden things sought up!
For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever.

In the day that thou stoodest on the other side, in the day that the strangers carried away captive his forces, and foreigners entered into his gates, and cast lots upon Jerusalem, even thou wast as one of them.
Thou also hast vowed to build up the temple, which the Edomites burned when Judea was made desolate by the Chaldees.

But thou shouldest not have looked on the day of thy brother in the day that he became a stranger; neither shouldest thou have rejoiced over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction; neither shouldest thou have spoken proudly in the day of distress.

Thou shouldest not have entered into the gate of my people in the day of their calamity; yea, thou shouldest not have looked on their affliction in the day of their calamity, nor have laid hands on their substance in the day of their calamity;
Neither shouldest thou have stood in the crossway, to cut off those of his that did escape; neither shouldest thou have delivered up those of his that did remain in the day of distress.
Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof.
Thus saith the Lord God; Because that Edom hath dealt against the house of Judah by taking vengeance, and hath greatly offended, and revenged himself upon them;

All the men of thy confederacy have brought thee even to the border: the men that were at peace with thee have deceived thee, and prevailed against thee; they that eat thy bread have laid a wound under thee: there is none understanding in him.
And the ten horns which thou sawest are ten kings, which have received no kingdom as yet; but receive power as kings one hour with the beast.
These have one mind, and shall give their power and strength unto the beast.
These shall make war with the Lamb, and the Lamb shall overcome them: for he is Lord of lords, and King of kings: and they that are with him are called, and chosen, and faithful.
And he saith unto me, The waters which thou sawest, where the whore sitteth, are peoples, and multitudes, and nations, and tongues.
And the ten horns which thou sawest upon the beast, these shall hate the whore, and shall make her desolate and naked, and shall eat her flesh, and burn her with fire.
For God hath put in their hearts to fulfil his will, and to agree, and give their kingdom unto the beast, until the words of God shall be fulfilled.
Shall I not in that day, saith the Lord, even destroy the wise men out of Edom, and understanding out of the mount of Esau?
And thy mighty men, O Teman, shall be dismayed, to the end that every one of the mount of Esau may be cut off by slaughter.
For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever.
For as ye have drunk upon my holy mountain, so shall all the heathen drink continually, yea, they shall drink, and they shall swallow down, and they shall be as though they had not been.
But upon mount Zion shall be deliverance, and there shall be holiness; and the house of Jacob shall possess their possessions.

And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble, and they shall kindle in them, and devour them; and there shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau; for the Lord hath spoken it.

Therefore thus saith the Lord God; I will also stretch out mine hand upon Edom, and will cut off man and beast from it; and I will make it desolate from Teman; and they of Dedan shall fall by the sword.

And I will lay my vengeance upon Edom by the hand of my people Israel: and they shall do in Edom according to mine anger and according to my fury; and they shall know my vengeance, saith the Lord God.
When I have bent Judah for me, filled the bow with Ephraim, and raised up thy sons, O Zion, against thy sons, O Greece, and made thee as the sword of a mighty man.
As gold in the furnace hath he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering.
And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble.
They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people, and their Lord shall reign for ever.
And saviours shall come up on mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau; and the kingdom shall be the Lord’s.

And the captivity of this host of the children of Israel shall possess that of the Canaanites, even unto Zarephath; and the captivity of Jerusalem, which is in Sepharad, shall possess the cities of the south.

O daughter of Babylon, who art to be destroyed; happy shall he be, that rewardeth thee as thou hast served us.
